title: Times table tricks
goal: I can use facts I know to find new times table facts. I can find patterns and solve number puzzles.

learn.intro: A times table fact you do not know can be built from facts you do know. Split a rectangle of dots into two smaller rectangles.

example.problem: There are 7 rows with 6 dots in each row. How many dots are there in all?
steps: The dashed line splits the dots into 5 rows and 2 rows.

howto.title: Ways to find a fact
steps: For 9 ×: take 1 group away from 10 groups.

try.text: There are 6 rows with 8 dots in each row. Split them into 3 rows and 3 rows. How many dots are there in all? {b}

items.text: Write the missing answers in the 8 times table.
items.explanation: The answers go up by 8 each time. 8 × 4 = 32, 8 × 6 = 48 and 8 × 9 = 72.

items.text: Write the answers.
items.explanation: 6 × 8 = 48, 7 × 9 = 63, 9 × 6 = 54 and 8 × 7 = 56. Swap the numbers to check: 8 × 6 = 48.

items.text: You know that 8 × 5 = 40. Use it to find the other facts.
items.explanation: (a) One more 8: 40 + 8 = 48. (b) One less 8: 40 - 8 = 32. (c) Double 8 × 5: 80. (d) 8 × 10 = 80, take away one 8: 72.

items.text: Ali packs 7 eggs in each box. He fills 9 boxes.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Then he packs 56 eggs into boxes of 7. He fills {b} boxes.

items.text: Find my number. It is in the 7 times table, and it is greater than 50 and less than 80. Its digits add up to 9. {b}
items.explanation: The numbers in the 7 times table between 50 and 80 are 56, 63, 70 and 77. Their digits add up to 11, 9, 7 and 14. Only 63 has digits that add up to 9.

items.text: The dashed line splits 7 rows of 9 dots into 2 parts.
Fill in the missing answers.
items.explanation: Each cell is the row number × the column number. A = 6 × 8 = 48. B = 7 × 6 = 42. C = 7 × 9 = 63. D = 8 × 7 = 56.

items.text: A row number times a column number makes each product. Write the missing numbers in the heading cells.
items.explanation: 54 and 63 are in the same row. Both are in the 9 times table: 54 = 9 × 6 and 63 = 9 × 7. So the row number is 9 and the columns are 6 and 7. The second row: 48 = 8 × 6 and 56 = 8 × 7, so the row number is 8.

items.text: Write the last digit of each answer. Do not find the whole answer.
items.explanation: Only the last digits matter. (a) 6 × 3 = 18 ends in 8. (b) 8 × 7 = 56 ends in 6. (c) 9 × 5 = 45 ends in 5. (d) 7 × 8 = 56 ends in 6.

items.text: Mei puts 30 tiles in equal rows. There are at least 2 rows and at least 2 tiles in each row. 2 rows of 15 and 15 rows of 2 are different ways. List ALL the ways.
items.explanation: Check the number of rows from 2 upwards: 2 rows of 15, 3 rows of 10, 5 rows of 6, 6 rows of 5, 10 rows of 3 and 15 rows of 2. 4 rows does not work because 30 is not in the 4 times table. That is 6 ways.
6 × 4 = 24, 6 × 7 = 42 and 6 × 10 = 60. The numbers 38 and 56 are not: 6 × 6 = 36 and 6 × 9 = 54, and the next answer after 54 is 60.

items.text: Mei buys 6 packs of 8 stickers. Ben buys 7 packs of 7 stickers.
items.explanation: Mei has 6 × 8 = 48 stickers. Ben has 7 × 7 = 49 stickers. Ben has 49 - 48 = 1 more.

items.text: Aisha says the 8 times table from 8 up to 96. How many of the numbers she says have an ODD tens digit? {b}
items.explanation: The numbers are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80, 88 and 96. The tens digits are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9. The odd ones are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9: so 16, 32, 56, 72 and 96. That is 5 numbers.
items.hint: Write the table first. Then look at the tens digits.

items.text: The row numbers and column numbers are all from 6 to 9. Find the empty cells A to D. You can write in the heading cells to help you.
items.explanation: 49 = 7 × 7, so row 2 and column 1 are both 7. Then 42 = 6 × 7 gives row 1 = 6, and 48 = 6 × 8 gives column 2 = 8. 63 = 7 × 9 gives column 3 = 9. 72 = 8 × 9 gives row 3 = 8. A = 6 × 9 = 54, B = 7 × 8 = 56, C = 8 × 7 = 56 and D = 8 × 8 = 64.
items.hint: Start with 49. Which row and column make 49?

items.text: Two numbers have a product of 63 and a sum of 16. What are the 2 numbers? {b} and {b}
items.explanation: The pairs that multiply to 63 are 1 and 63, 3 and 21, 7 and 9. Their sums are 64, 24 and 16. Only 7 and 9 add up to 16.
items.hint: List the pairs of numbers that multiply to make 63.
Add the digits of each number. Keep adding until 1 digit is left.

items.text: A hall has 8 rows. Row 1 has 7 seats. Each row has 2 more seats than the row before.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The hall has {b} seats in all.

items.explanation: The seats go 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 21. Row 8 has 21 seats. Pair them: 7 + 21 = 28, 9 + 19 = 28, 11 + 17 = 28, 13 + 15 = 28. There are 4 pairs, so 4 × 28 = 112 seats.
items.hint: Pair the first and last rows. Then the next pair.

items.text: Make your own 2 by 2 grid puzzle with numbers from 6 to 9. Show 3 products. Only ONE answer may fit. Swap it with a grown-up.

answer.text: Answers vary. Example: the products 42, 48 and 49 are shown. The row numbers are 6 and 7 and the column numbers are 7 and 8, so the hidden product is 56.

items.explanation: Check that each shown product belongs to the numbers you chose. Check that no other row and column numbers from 6 to 9 give the same 3 products. In the example, 42 = 6 × 7 and 48 = 6 × 8 give row 6 and columns 7 and 8. Also 49 = 7 × 7 gives row 7. The hidden product is 7 × 8 = 56.
items.hint: Pick the row and column numbers first. Then multiply.

items.text:
Multiply a number by itself. For example 7 × 7 = 49, which ends in 9. Which of these digits can NEVER end such an answer?
{circ:2|3|4|6|7|8}
items.explanation: The last digits of 1 × 1 up to 9 × 9 are 1, 4, 9, 6, 5, 6, 9, 4, 1. Only the last digit of the number matters, so the last digit can only be 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9. So 2, 3, 7 and 8 can never be the last digit.

items.text: A box holds 8 pens. How many pens are in 7 boxes? {b}
You know that 10 × 8 = 80. Use it to find 9 × 8. {b}
items.explanation: 9 × 8 is one less 8 than 10 × 8: 80 - 8 = 72.

items.text: Is 63 in the 6 times table?   {circ:Yes|No}
items.explanation: 6 × 10 = 60 and 6 × 11 = 66, so 63 is not in the table.

items.text: Mei has 54 apples. She puts 6 apples in each bag. How many bags does she need? {b}
